releases.title: A selected state for menus, and retuned themes
body: Menu items can now show a current choice. Give the items of a DropdownMenu or ContextMenu a selected value and they become a set of radio items: the chosen one holds a quiet fill, full-strength text and icon, and a trailing check. Plain action items are unchanged.

Three theme presets take new typeface pairings: Bubblegum sets Fredoka over Nunito, Velvet sets Playfair Display over Plus Jakarta Sans, and Volt sets Space Grotesk over Manrope, with the faces shipped in the package. Tinted themes are brighter in light mode, where the two lightest surfaces carry half the tint they did. The Fraunces and Work Sans font files leave the package, since no preset uses them. Nothing else is removed, so upgrading needs no code changes.

releases.title: File attachments for chat
body: Four new components for files in a conversation. AttachmentTile draws one file as a square: a picture fills it, a PDF, spreadsheet, document or presentation wears a coloured mark, and every other file wears its extension as a neutral badge. AttachmentGroup lays out the files on a sent message, AttachmentViewer opens them in a preview dialog, and AttachmentDropZone lets a file be dropped anywhere on a chat. A headless hook, useAttachments, owns the list of files and their previews.

Composer now takes files: an attach button, paste and drop feed a row of tiles above the input, and a message can be files alone. ChatMessage shows a turn's files above its bubble. Four new file-format colour tokens keep the colour each format is known by in every theme. DocumentChip is deprecated in favour of the tile and keeps working. Nothing breaks, so upgrading needs no code changes.

releases.title: InspectorColorPicker and the action colour
body: InspectorColorPicker joins the Inspector family: the library colour picker dressed as one bar, with its name on the left and the colour on the right. A new motion token, the orbit duration, paces Globe's spin, so a theme's motion scale now reaches it, and Composer can place its context note above the input with contextPlacement="above".

The action colour is now kept for actions. Spinner, FileInput, Sparkline, the bar charts, Timeline's links, Instructions and DatePicker's today ring each use the role that fits instead, and a build check stops new decorative uses. Every action fill also holds contrast with its label and icon in every state, which repairs the Volt preset, and Treemap labels pick a readable colour for each cell. Nothing breaks, so upgrading needs no code changes.

releases.title: The Inspector family
body: Six one-row controls for tool panels and settings rails: InspectorSlider, InspectorInput, InspectorToggleSwitch, InspectorSegmentedControl, InspectorDropdown, and InspectorSection to group them. Each is one bar with its name inside, sized and shaped like Button, so a dense panel of settings stays light. They sit beside the form controls rather than replacing them.
SegmentedControl's track corner now counts its hairline, so on a theme with squarer pills it stays parallel with the sliding pill. Nothing breaks, so upgrading needs no code changes.

releases.title: Mobile app navigation
body: Three new navigation components. BottomNav is the tab bar of a mobile app, drawn in the Rift style, as the iOS Liquid Glass capsule, or as the Material 3 Expressive bar. TopAppBar is the header of a mobile screen, with a title that collapses as the page scrolls. SidebarPanel lists one section's pages, on its own or beside AppSidebar as a third navigation level.

Screen readers get more to work with: charts are named by their title, Nav names its landmark and accepts native props, and Stepper announces its steps. Nothing breaks, so upgrading needs no code changes.

releases.title: A readable package page
body: No code changed. 1.0.0 shipped with the README's banner image as a relative path, which npm cannot resolve against the repository, so the package page opened with a broken image. This release carries an absolute one.
The banner is now generated from the repository URL rather than typed by hand, alongside the npm badge that already worked that way, so it cannot drift again.

releases.title: The first Rift DS release
body: Rift DS is on npm. `npm install rift-ds` gets you 133 React components built on 255 semantic design tokens, with light and dark modes in the box and React as the only required peer dependency.

Theming is plain CSS custom properties. There is no provider to mount and no config file to write: every semantic token chains to a primitive, so overriding a handful of primitives restyles everything built on them, the charts and the ambient background included. Eleven complete themes ship as generated stylesheets, and setting one `data-brand` attribute on the root element applies a whole look, self-hosted typefaces and all, with no runtime JavaScript.
The Recharts-backed charts live behind their own entry point, so `recharts` stays an optional peer dependency you install only if you use them.

Coding agents are treated as first-class consumers. `npx rift-ds init` installs an agent skill into your project and prints the MCP connect line, and the public MCP endpoint serves the component catalogue, the prop contracts and the token registry with no key and no account. All of it is generated from the same JSDoc that builds the shipped type declarations, so an agent reads the exact contract the package ships.
Prefer owning the source? Every component is also installable through the shadcn CLI, or you can clone the repo. All three paths are MIT.
If you were using the earlier scoped package, this is the same system under its own name. Change your import specifier to `rift-ds` and nothing else moves.

predecessorReleases.summary: The package’s first bin: an init command that fetches the consumer agent skill from the live site into .claude/skills/ and prints the MCP connect line.

Six components taking the registry to 132: WorldMap, the flat companion to Globe, plus Toolbar, Lightbox, Waveform, AnimatedNumber and StatusDot. Lightbox is the first overlay born on the shared behaviour layer, and the count-up budget joins the motion constants.

GanttChart and RichDropdown, the heading and body font family roles for split-face theming, AiButton’s signature refresh, Dropdown’s typeface preview, the micro-animation pass (SegmentedControl’s sliding pill, Button’s trailing-icon nudge), and ToggleSwitch labels hugging the track.

The section-divider rhythm fix. SectionTitle’s rule clearance drops so every divider header runs heading, 20px, rule, 40px, content, and the rule width and Table’s hairlines move onto the border tokens.

ThreadTabs, the animated strip of open chat sessions, with ThreadPanel’s detail rows, pin marks and projects section; PromptSuggestions’ pending shimmer and entrance stagger; and CommandPalette’s trailing slot for a non-interactive row badge.

ThreadPanel, the session-history rail for chat products, plus EventCalendar’s selectedDate and whole-cell interactivity on its own calendar colour family, and the toast exit timer on the motion constant.

The shared overlay behaviour layer under the modal components, with useScrollLock published for host chrome. Also AiButton’s summary panel, Composer’s context note, the status icon step tokens, and overlay listener and timer fixes.

UsageCard and SourceTrail join the ai category, and Composer gains its working glow. The agent-docs surfaces arrive around the package: per-component markdown contracts, the consumer agent skill, and the MCP roster with example prompts.

Six components taking the registry to 120: Banner, HoverCard, ImageCompare, Meter, Rating and SplitButton, plus LinkList’s newTab opt-out. The same JSDoc now also feeds the site’s public MCP endpoint.
Five composition gap-fillers: Gauge, FilterBar, SplitPane, StreamingText and AvatarGroup, plus the stream reveal’s motion constant and the amended JS motion contract.

The dashboard set from the labs rebuild: Panel, LegendTile, FunnelChart and ComboChart, with live var() chart colours and bare mode, Stat’s trend tokens and inline delta, borderless badges, and AppSidebar’s floating variant, item badges, slots and rebuilt transition.
The maps category (Globe, MapCallout, MapLegend), plus CardStack and the overline typography face.

The accessible teal split: the action colour becomes theme-dependent, a deep light-mode fill inverting to a light dark-mode one, with every action pairing at WCAG AA. Also SectionTitle’s optional divider and AppSidebar link rows.

Nine components taking the registry past 100: AnchorNav plus Stepper, TagInput, NumberInput, TreeView, PinInput, CodeDiff, Sparkline and TimePicker. The published dist also gets its ‘use client’ directives back.
Five components from the dashboard gap analysis: AgentPlan, ModelPicker, NotificationCenter, DataTable and EventCalendar.
ShaderField, the WebGL2 ambient background, with Card’s cover slot and the instant motion duration token.
The composer radius token, ChatMessage’s showActions, and a README that states the chat’s UI-only boundary.
The chat component set that powers the site-wide chat.
The ai component category.
The first release through Trusted Publishing, authenticated by OIDC with no token.
The first publish, using a granular npm token that has since been retired.
